morning.insight:
💡 「수요일의 시작: 밀린 짐 + 메가 위크」

어제 KOSPI가 3.73% 급락하며 전일 반등분을 전부 반납했습니다. 5,552.74는 7,000선 붕괴(9/14) 후 형성된 5,400~5,800 박스권의 하단에 근접한 수준입니다. 외국인·기관 동반 순매도 속에서 개인이 홀로 9천억을 사들이고 있는데 — 개인 투자자들의 '바닥 인식' 매수가 강하지만, 기관의 이탈 속도가 더 빠릅니다.

**오늘은 '메가 위크'의 정점**입니다. 엔비디아 GTC 베를린(젠슨 황 기조연설), 테슬라·메타 실적, 내일 한은 금통위까지 — 글로벌 자산가격 방향을 결정할 48시간입니다. 특히 테슬라 실적과 엔비디아 GTC 발표는 AI 투자 정당성 논쟁의 분수령이 될 수 있습니다. KOSPI 반도체주(삼성전자·SK하이닉스)의 방향도 여기에 달려 있습니다.

**콕핏: ZAIC 내일 + New-Z 오늘**
내일(22일) 제2회 ZAIC 성과발표회가 있습니다. 2차 심사결과 보고(밀린 일)가 아직 안 끝났습니다 — 오전에 처리하고 New-Z 웰컴데이 강의를 준비하세요. Z-P3 전략기획실 세부사업계획서 중간 리뷰회의도 오늘 중 리뷰입니다.

**오늘 체크리스트**
- [ ] [T-P9] ZAIC 2차 심사결과 보고서 제출 (내일 행사, 긴급)
- [ ] [T-P7] New-Z 웰컴데이 강의 실시 (오늘)
- [ ] [Z-P3] 전략기획실 팀별 사업계획서 중간 리뷰회의
- [ ] [Z-P6] AX 도입 검토 1차 보고서 초안 (지연 해소)
- [ ] [T-P13] 2027년 기획자료·업무리스트 업데이트
- [ ] Anthropic $220 환불 — Fin AI Agent 회신 확인·후속조치
- [ ] NVIDIA GTC 베를린 젠슨 황 기조연설 체크 (저녁 이후 미국 시간)
- [ ] 테슬라·메타 실적 장 마감 후 모니터링 (내일 브리핑 반영)

articles.headline: 코스피 5,400~5,800 박스권 하단 위협…7거래일 연속 하락 후 재추락
articles.eng: Kospi threatens lower end of 5,400-5,800 range after renewed slide
articles.body: 코스피가 5,552.74로 마감하며 7,000선 붕괴(9/14) 후 형성된 5,400~5,800 박스권의 하단을 위협하고 있다. 일시 반등 뒤 다시 추락한 모양새다.

articles.headline: SpaceX Reports Profit as Revenue Doubles
articles.body: SpaceX reported a profit as revenue doubled in its second set of results since going public, a closely watched read on whether the AI-investment boom remains on solid ground.

articles.headline: Dow Rallies 530 Points to a One-Month High as Oil Slides
articles.body: The Dow jumped 1.02% to 52,495.88, its best close in about a month, helped by falling oil prices and earnings-season optimism, while the S&P 500 rose 0.28% and the Nasdaq finished nearly flat.

articles.headline: The Surge in Rates Is Blowing Up Commercial Real Estate
articles.body: Rising interest rates are straining commercial real estate borrowers, stoking fears of a debt bomb as refinancing costs climb across the sector.

articles.headline: Tesla, Meta Earnings Loom Over the AI Trade
articles.body: Investors are bracing for Tesla and Meta earnings as the two reports test whether the AI capital-spending cycle can keep justifying itself after last week's selloff.

articles.headline: Midterm Anxiety Mounts for GOP as Democrats Expand Battleground
articles.body: Republican anxiety is rising ahead of the midterms as Democrats press into once-safe territory, buoyed by President Trump's low approval ratings.

articles.headline: Inflation Keeps Biting Real Wages
articles.body: Sticky inflation continues to erode real wages, adding to pressure on the Federal Reserve to keep policy tight.

articles.headline: Boeing Wins Approval for Largest Variant of Its 737 Max Jet
articles.body: Boeing won certification for the 737 MAX 10, capping a lengthy saga for the narrowbody family disrupted by two fatal crashes and a series of quality lapses.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Huang Says AI Market Turmoil 'Will Pass'
articles.body: Jensen Huang took a sanguine view of the AI stock-market rout, saying the technology's benefits will soon outweigh investor concerns and 'all of this is going to pass.'

articles.headline: SoftBank Credit Risk Hits Four-Year High on AI Funding Strain
articles.body: SoftBank's five-year credit default swaps widened to the highest since late 2022 as worries grow over AI spending funded by borrowing.

articles.headline: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent Place $35 Billion in Nvidia Chip Orders
articles.body: Chinese tech giants have placed more than $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders, underscoring enduring demand for AI accelerators despite the market turmoil.

articles.headline: South Korea Set to Hold Rates Before November Hike, Economists Say
articles.body: The Bank of Korea is expected to keep its key rate at 3.00% on Thursday after two straight increases, before raising it again in November as inflation stays above target.

articles.headline: Jamie Dimon Says US Economy Strong, Warns of War and Inflation Risks
articles.body: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon called the U.S. economy strong but flagged overseas conflicts, budget shortfalls and sticky inflation as key risks.

articles.headline: With Trump's Plans Blocked, States Work to Restore Trust in Mail Voting
articles.body: President Trump's efforts to restrict mail voting were thwarted by the Supreme Court, but they have sown confusion and doubt among some voters ahead of the midterms.

articles.headline: Democrats Gain Edge as Trump Drags Down G.O.P., New Poll Finds
articles.body: Even some Republicans are losing faith in Trump's economy, a New York Times/Siena poll found, as Democrats gain an edge on top issues heading into the midterms.

articles.headline: U.S. Health Officials Move Quickly to Deploy Medical A.I. Despite Concerns
articles.body: Federal projects are rolling out A.I. agents that offer therapy and prescribe medicine, raising concerns about safety and the influence of venture capital investors.

articles.headline: Rising Fuel Prices Set Off Anger and Protests Around the World
articles.body: From Indonesia to Guatemala to Syria, shortages and price increases are leading to protests and blackouts.

articles.headline: Trump Campaigns for Republicans as Turmoil Mounts in Washington
articles.body: President Trump campaigned across the country to shore up Republicans ahead of the midterms, even as turmoil mounted in his administration.

articles.headline: Bill Gates's Blunt Warning on A.I.
articles.body: Bill Gates offered a blunt assessment of artificial intelligence's risks and potential, cautioning that the technology's downsides demand serious attention.

articles.headline: NFL says heightened security will be in place for Steelers-Saints game in Paris
articles.body: The NFL said security will be heightened for the Paris game after civil unrest protests engulfed the French capital last weekend.

articles.headline: Pentagon raises official toll of troops who died during war with Iran to 21
articles.body: The Pentagon raised the official toll of U.S. troops who died during the war with Iran to 21, as officials face scrutiny over undisclosed casualties.

articles.headline: Home heating oil is a sleeper campaign issue across cold-weather battlegrounds
articles.body: Rising heating costs have become a quiet but potent campaign issue in cold-weather swing districts ahead of the midterms.

articles.headline: On AI risks, the U.S. and China should work together
articles.body: The most important global race isn't simply for AI dominance but for safeguards before capabilities outrun them, an opinion piece argues.

articles.headline: CNN, MS NOW, Politico say journalists blocked from White House after Trump announces ban
articles.body: News outlets and press advocacy groups condemned the move as a violation of the First Amendment after President Trump moved to block several outlets from White House grounds.

articles.headline: Trump approval hits record low, handing Democrats a clear midterm edge
articles.body: President Trump's approval rating fell to a record low, giving Democrats a clear advantage heading into the midterms.

articles.headline: US stocks recover after AI sell-off
articles.body: US equities clawed back ground after the previous week's AI-driven rout, though the rebound proved narrow and concentrated in a handful of names.

articles.headline: South Korea expected to hold rates on Oct 22, hike in November
articles.body: The Bank of Korea is set to hold its policy rate at 3.00% this week before raising borrowing costs once more next month, a Reuters poll of economists found.

articles.headline: Tesla and Meta earnings put the AI trade to the test
articles.body: Results from Tesla and Meta this week are a key stress test for whether heavy AI spending can translate into profitability.

articles.headline: Oil slides as Qatar-Pakistan peace proposal raises hopes
articles.body: Brent crude retreated from multi-week highs after reports of a Qatar-Pakistan mediation proposal aimed at easing Middle East tensions.

articles.headline: Microsoft pulls plug on Nscale data centre deal
articles.body: Microsoft withdrew from a UK data-centre deal with Nscale, adding to concerns about cooling demand for AI capacity.

articles.headline: SoftBank CDS hit highest since 2022 on AI funding strain
articles.body: SoftBank's credit default swaps widened to their highest since late 2022 as markets fret over debt-funded AI investment.
